summary: All 30 records tests rerun successfully, but an independent actual public-boundary probe falsifies admission through a supported symlink path. With a pinned reader and canonical WAL backlog, alias admission measured only 6328320 bytes, accepted a limit of 13340240, and returned saved:5 while canonical DB+WAL+SHM occupied 15952480. SQLite uses real-path auxiliary files; lexical caller-path suffixes silently undercount them. A no-reader counterfactual checkpointed on last close and did not expose this defect. Reject P02; correct effective database identity/accounting or explicitly refuse unsupported paths before writes, with behavioral RED and held-reader regression. No new architecture or weaker quota policy is requested.

observation.counterfactual: Hold a real read snapshot to preserve WAL backlog. Earlier no-reader attempt allowed last-close checkpoint and did not expose overshoot. Two canonical writes build backlog before alias admission.
